upstream.label: is interrupted when scope is closed

cases.behavior: Closing an owning scope interrupts its child and waits for child cleanup before parent cleanup.
cases.limits: The Effra fixture asserts completed child-before-parent release, not upstream Scope internals or the entire forkScoped API.

upstream.label: scoped combines usage and finalizer failures

cases.behavior: An expected failure and a cleanup defect both survive scope closure.
cases.limits: Effra uses Timeout plus an acquired-resource cleanup defect, including attempted Timeout recovery. This is a behavior comparison, not a port of generic addFinalizer syntax.

upstream.label: sleep - does not require passage of wall time

cases.behavior: Advancing test program time admits an already-forked sleeper and allows its join without waiting for the requested wall-clock delay.
cases.limits: Effra tests explicit TestClock/TestScheduler providers and an admitted but unstarted fork at 36000000 milliseconds (10 hours), under a 15-second watchdog per target; they do not assert all TestClock adjustment/precision behavior.

cases.behavior: A deadline reports a typed timeout; a timer defect must retain its Cause rather than being recast as that timeout.
cases.limits: Upstream asserts Cause.TimeoutError with a duration message. Effra declares nominal Timeout and an explicit Scheduler capability; its supplemental invalid-duration timer test also checks cleanup defects. This does not claim identical timeout APIs or full upstream case parity.

cases.behavior: Interrupt during protected acquisition skips use but releases the acquired resource.
cases.limits: Generic source-level acquisition callback contracts and causal acquisition-boundary acceptance remain future owned-core work; existing lifecycle providers are not this proof.

cases.behavior: The first completion wins; repeated completion returns false and waiters see the first value.
cases.limits: An internal latch is not an admitted generic Effra Deferred API. Recipe execution/memoization is separate from single assignment and does not imply concurrent producer single-flight.

cases.behavior: A Ref read returns its current stored value.
cases.limits: Generic mutable payload ownership and callback purity admission remain required; native cells alone are not source-level conformance.

upstream.label: withPermits interruption does not leak permits

cases.behavior: Interrupting queued permit acquisition does not consume or leak permits.
cases.limits: Future fixed-capacity Semaphore must add causal queued/handoff/cancel tests. PartitionedSemaphore and resize/manual release cases do not establish that first profile.
Effra's admitted owned cleanup is sequential; no selectable parallel scope-finalization policy is exposed.

cases.behavior: A detached child outlives interruption of its parent.
cases.limits: Effra's first profile requires an owning scope; detached fibers remain unsupported.

cases.behavior: A JSON string decodes to a string and non-strings fail with a typed first issue.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes.

cases.behavior: JSON true/false decode to booleans; other JSON values fail.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes.

cases.behavior: Void decodes only from a present JSON null, fails on any other value or a missing key, and encodes as JSON null.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes. Effra's void boundary, absence and host-null contracts are unchanged; only the codec representation is compared.

cases.behavior: A signed decimal string decodes to a 64-bit integer with leading zeros and negative zero normalized; non-decimal strings fail.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes. The signed 64-bit range is an added comparator check, not upstream BigInt behavior.

upstream.label: applies excess-property options to unmatched own keys

cases.behavior: Record and variant decoding ignore excess properties under the default policy.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes. Only the ignore policy is profiled; error and preserve are not offered.

upstream.label: use case: create a JSON string serializer for an existing schema

cases.behavior: Decoding a JSON string into a struct reports a missing declared key at its path; malformed text fails as a JSON parse failure.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes.

cases.behavior: Effra admission is stricter than JSON.parse: duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, lone surrogate escapes, byte-order marks, and body/depth bounds fail with byte offsets where Effect parses last-wins over replacement-decoded text without bounds.
cases.limits: Executed by conformance/codecs/effect-comparator.mjs over the shared effra/json-structural-1 policy vectors; the vector test compares Go and JS outcomes with the retained comparator bytes. Each differing vector is labelled `difference` in json-structural-vectors.json.

upstream.label: interrupting a build does not hang current or later requesters

cases.behavior: Interrupting one requester of a shared layer acquisition leaves other current and later requesters able to complete.
cases.limits: Upstream MemoMap builds in the first requester's fiber, so interrupting it completes the shared entry with that interruption for every waiter. Effra producers belong to the provision build: cancelling one waiter abandons only its own wait, the producer continues, and every other waiter observes the actual shared outcome. Whole-build cancellation is the only static-surface trigger; the evidence drives the emitted Go runtime and JavaScript layer runtime seam directly until a language caller exists.
